citation: Monte AA, Bucher-Bartelson B, Heard KJ. A US perspective of symptomatic Latrodectus spp. envenomation and treatment: a National Poison Data System review.
population_or_context: US symptomatic Latrodectus exposures reported to NPDS
evidence_role: Primary quantitative severity source for black-widow false-negative harm
key_extracted_evidence: Black widow envenomation is clinically significant in the US; the review is the source cited by StatPearls for 23,409 exposures, with most symptomatic cases minor but a substantial moderate treatment-requiring group and rare major life-threatening effects.
uncertainty_or_limits: Poison-center data depend on reporting and exposure classification; applies to envenomation consequences rather than pure image identification.

citation: Williams M, Sehgal N, Nappe TM. Black Widow Spider Toxicity. StatPearls.
evidence_role: Clinical mapping from black widow identity to urgency, morbidity, and treatment burden
key_extracted_evidence: Describes Latrodectus as responsible for most clinically significant spider envenomation in the US; latrodectism can include diffuse pain, muscle rigidity, autonomic findings, and treatment with opioids, benzodiazepines, observation, toxicology consultation, and antivenom in selected cases.
uncertainty_or_limits: Clinical review, not a formal cost-utility study; cites registry literature but does not provide a decision threshold.

citation: Barish RA, Arnold T. Spider Bites. Merck Manual Professional Edition.
population_or_context: Professional clinical summary of spider bites
evidence_role: Independent clinical corroboration of high-cost black-widow miss
key_extracted_evidence: Widow bites can progress within an hour to persistent pain and systemic symptoms; moderate and severe latrodectism are clinically recognized; treatment can include parenteral opioids, benzodiazepines, antivenom, and toxicology consultation.
uncertainty_or_limits: General clinical reference; not specific to the image dataset and not numeric cost evidence.

citation: Graudins A, Gunja N, Broady KW, Nicholson GM. Clinical and in vitro evidence for the efficacy of Australian red-back spider antivenom in the treatment of envenomation by a Cupboard spider (Steatoda grossa).
population_or_context: Steatoda grossa envenomation case and venom/antivenom evidence
evidence_role: Bounds false-widow harm above zero while below Latrodectus-level public-health concern
key_extracted_evidence: Steatoda grossa can cause clinically meaningful steatodism in rare cases, so a false-widow false alarm should not be treated as costless; however the evidence base is case-level rather than registry-level.
uncertainty_or_limits: Single-case/case-level evidence; species and geography may not match all false-widow images.

citation: University of California IPM. Widow Spiders and Their Relatives.
evidence_role: Decision-context evidence that false widows resemble true widows but are not equivalent medically
key_extracted_evidence: False black widow Steatoda grossa is visually confusable with widow spiders; public guidance emphasizes true widow medical aspects and management.
uncertainty_or_limits: Extension guidance is not medical outcome data; useful for context, not numeric derivation alone.

citation: Montana State University Extension IPM. Cob-web Weavers (Steatoda).
evidence_role: Corroborates that false-widow identification errors mostly drive caution or evaluation rather than Latrodectus-level morbidity
key_extracted_evidence: Describes Steatoda false widows as close relatives and common household spiders, supporting image-confusion relevance and lower expected harm for false-positive black-widow alerts.
uncertainty_or_limits: Not a clinical outcomes source; used only as low-cost-error context.

exclusion_reason: Excluded from numeric derivation because it is non-authoritative background, although it may be useful for lay terminology.
key_extracted_evidence: Useful for common names but not reliable enough for scoring or ratio derivation.

key_extracted_evidence: May reflect public anxiety but cannot quantify either medical harm or cost ratio.
